that answers one question: which of my sessions needs

Recorded from the window itself (--record), frame by frame — not a mock-up.
## Why

If you run more than a couple of sessions, finding out whether anything is waiting on you costs a
co
ntext switch every time:
| what you do today | what it costs |

| alt-tab between windows and read each sidebar | the thing you were doing, every time |
| wait for

a desktop notification | one per session, and none of them say which one is *blocked* |
| leave the
sidebar visible | it is only visible when the app is in front — which is when you do not need it |
The notch is a small always-on-top tab that **never takes focus**, **hides under a full-screen app**

, and
shows the one thing the sidebar cannot while you are in another window: **a session stuck on y

ou**. When
one gets stuck, the tab grows into an alert that says why, with an **Open** button that s

witches the app
to that session — from wherever it is, minimized or in the tray. And it **never gets

in the way**:
pass over it and it fades and lets your click through; rest on it and the board unfol

the way**:
pass over it and it fades and lets your click through; rest on it and the board unfolds.
## What it shows
That strip is the whole visual language. **Working** wears a slow blue arc and nothing else, because
working is the quiet default — and while any session is running a tool, light runs along the tab's

lower
edge. **Needs you** wears amber, **done** green, **failed** red. Every session keeps its own c

olour on the
bot's rim, so three sessions read as three sessions rather than three copies of one.
### It never gets in the way
The tab sits where you reach for tabs and title bars, so it steps aside. A pointer **passing over**

it
turns it into a faint ghost that clicks go straight through — to the browser tab or the menu unde

r it.
Only a pointer that **rests** there for 1.6 s unfolds the board, and pushing it against the to

p edge of
the screen opens it at once. All three are settings (`hoverMode`, `holdMs`, `topEdgeOpens`

); `open`
brings back unfold-on-hover.
### The tab speaks up
When something **new** happens — a session asks for you, fails, or finishes — the tab grows into an
alert for a few seconds and then folds back. **Open** takes you straight to that session. Only fresh
events are announced: a question that has been waiting for an hour is on the board, not in your fac
vents are announced: a question that has been waiting for an hour is on the board, not in your face.
### The board
Rest the pointer on the tab, or push it against the top of the screen, and the board unfolds. At the

top is the session that **changed most recently**, so a
finish or a question is what you see first:

its title, its project and age, how full its context is, and
one line of what it is doing — the too

l it is running and the step, the question it is asking in full,
or how it ended. Below it, every ot

her session in one list: what it is doing in a word and how long ago.
More sessions than fit? The li

in one list: what it is doing in a word and how long ago.
More sessions than fit? The list scrolls.
**Click** a row to put that session on the big bot. **Double-click** a row, or press **Open ↗**, and

the
app switches to it. A finished or failed row has a **✕** that closes it out — the same as ticki

to it. A finished or failed row has a **✕** that closes it out — the same as ticking it in
the app.
### Sixteen faces
The bot's face is the state, read closer. A working bot is **focused** in a tool and **thinking** be

tween
tools, **determined** on a long busy turn and **tired** after half an hour; it is **confused**

when a tool
just failed and **dizzy** when they keep failing. It **pleads** when it needs you, squi

nts `^^` when it is
done, and falls **asleep** when the host goes quiet. It blinks, follows your poi

nter with its eyes, and
plays a short motion on each change — once, and then it rests. A board that

keeps celebrating something
that finished an hour ago is noise.
**🫥 Never in the way**

Never takes focus, and steps aside when you pass over it: it fades and your click goes through.
No s
hadow on your desktop. Hides under a full-screen app.
**↗️ Open goes there**
Open, or a double-click, switches DeepSeek Harness to that session and brings it to the front — out

of
the taskbar or the tray.
**📏 Honest numbers**

## Requirements
- **Windows 10/11, x64.** The window is WPF and Win32 (topmost, no-activate, fullscreen detection):

there is no macOS or Linux build. `package.json` declares `"os": ["win32"]`.
- **DeepSeek Harness.**

Built and verified on **0.2.1-rc.2**. The host half reads `session/event`
(`{ global: true }`), `ct

x.webServer`, `ctx.agents` and `sessionQuery`, and the in-app half uses
`uiWorkspace`; an older buil

d may lack one. Nothing is checked before mounting — see
*Limits*.
- **Node ≥ 22** for the plugin. *

*No .NET runtime**: the released window is self-contained.
- Optional: the **`session-finished`** pl

ugin, which is what retires a finished row
(*What earns a row*).
## What earns a row

A session is on the board because **something happened to it**: it is working, it is blocked on an
a

pproval or a question, it failed, or it finished and you have not closed it out. Merely being open
n
ever earns a row, however many sessions are attached.

Finished and failed rows do not expire on a timer. They leave when the harness's own close-out
verdi

ct says so — the ✓ that the **`session-finished`** plugin puts in the sidebar, read over that
plugin

's HTTP route, or the ✕ on the row. If that plugin is not installed, this one notices after three
fa

iled probes and retires settled rows after 15 minutes instead, and says so in its report
(`host-repo

and retires settled rows after 15 minutes instead, and says so in its report
(`host-report.jsonl`).
When the host stops answering, the board stops pretending — the tab goes grey, the bot falls asleep,
and the sub line dates the last heartbeat instead of repeating a summary nobody is updating:
